rationale:
Evidence: the best design so far (iteration 6, score 138.6) has 5 sensors at y=0.08 with a +/-0.05 m span, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], base_speed 1.0, kp 4.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.6. Across the 60 development trials of that design, the oval had 1 finish in 20, s-bend progress was 0.295 (up from 0.156 at y=0.07), and slalom progress was 0.097. The main remaining problems are that every run still leaves the line (max error ~0.062 m against a 0.06 m limit), the s-bend logs 1.25 line-loss events per run, and oval steering oscillation is 0.30. Line loss on bends suggests that at larger offsets no sensor sees the tape, so the signal drops out. Forward placement at y=0.08 is already at the contract maximum, so the remaining lever is lateral coverage.

Changes: (1) widen the sensor span to x = -0.07 to +0.07 m in 0.035 m steps, so the tape stays under a sensor at larger offsets and line loss on bends should fall; (2) keep the 16 mm footprint and 5 sensors; (3) weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] are kept, which lowers the signal slope from about 40 to about 29 per metre, so kp rises from 4.0 to 5.0 to restore correction strength per centimetre; (4) ki 0.5, kd 0.6 and base_speed 1.0 are unchanged, since these are the settings that produced the only oval finishes; (5) wheel track, radius, body and mass are unchanged.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events (toward 0.5 or less on the s-bend), progress above 0.3 on the s-bend and slalom, and more oval completions. A full finish on the s-bend or slalom is unlikely this round. If the robot still exits at a fixed point, the next race should point to the kd term or to the speed.
